messages:
kevin: Heads-up — saw customer A's console showing runs from customer B when switching workspaces quickly. Not a UI render glitch, actual run rows are wrong. cc @raj @olivia
raj: ugh. can you paste the request headers / an example run id?
kevin: here's a sanitized request I grabbed from packet capture: `GET /console/api/runs?workspace=ws-A`
    Headers:
    `Authorization: Bearer tok_user:org-A`
    `X-Workspace: ws-A`
    `X-Org: org-B`
    `X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.1.5`
olivia: wait, X-Org says org-B while token says org-A? how is X-Org getting set to B?
maria: could be a proxy rewrite lingering from earlier route. we had a kube-ingress change last week that adds `x-org` for service-to-service calls.
sre-oncall: telemetry shows ~0.02% of console requests this week where `x-org` != token org. not huge but enough to confuse small number of users. logs attached to the alert: `console-authz-mismatch-2024-07-18`
kevin: reproducer steps: 1) open ws-A, 2) rapidly switch to ws-B and back with the quick-switcher, 3) sometimes the list endpoint returns rows from B while filters indicate A.
raj: suspect: session-mapper middleware prefers header `X-Org` when present and only falls back to token if missing. If tenant header is allowed from internal calls, external requests can be poisoned via proxy path.
devex: that matches a report from a customer on Friday. they used a CDN with a header rewrite rule. not all proxies strip `X-Org` by default.
olivia: immediate mitigation: force-strip `X-Org` at the edge for unauthenticated/edge-facing routes. add a guard in the auth gateway: if incoming token org != X-Org then drop header.
sre-oncall: I'll add a WAF rule to drop `X-Org` from internet-facing LB now. want a code fix too though.
maria: quick patch idea in `session-mapper`: assert `header_org == token_org` else log+ignore header. minimal risk. PR?
kevin: opened draft PR: `platform#4821` with test that simulates header mismatch. Includes a telemetry counter `auth.header_mismatch.count`.
raj: long-term, we should audit every internal header we accept and lock them behind mTLS/internal-only. Also add an integration test that runs quick-switch race scenarios against mock proxies.
devex: UX note — customers saw orphaned runs in their workspace list; we should send a short customer-facing note if this impacted any orgs with hits > 0.1% of their requests. ops-sig?
deploy-bot: deploy `auth-gateway` rollback to v3.9.1 queued for 1m.
kevin: timeline: WAF in place now, PR in review, will roll the gateway change canary to 5% then 100% after +24h.
raj: also add assertion in console backend query layer: require `WHERE org_id = token_org` even if header provided. Defensive DB-level scoping.
olivia: agreed. also add an alert for `auth.header_mismatch.count >= 5/min` per org so we catch proxy misconfigs.
sre-oncall: creating incident doc: `INC-2024-07-18-console-cred-shadow` with timeline + remediation steps.
maria: thanks everyone. action items: WAF rule (sre), PR review + canary (kevin/raj), DB defensive check (olivia), customer outreach draft (devex).
kevin: small log snippet I grabbed:
```
WARN auth: header org (org-B) != token org (org-A) request_id=abcd1234 route=/api/runs
```
kevin: will follow-up when canary is healthy. :thumbsup:
devex: can we also add a short note in the console release notes about stricter header handling so customers expecting to pass org headers for internal integrations know the change?
raj: yes, include migration docs and a config knob for on-prem/private where customers may intentionally set headers from a trusted network.
kevin: ok wrapping — thanks all.
